note: What a server answers a registration with, naming a player in the match and the seat they occupy. It shares its command value with the request it answers, which travels the other way, and it is one fixed size: a server sends one for every seat, whether that seat has just registered or was already at the match.

fields.name: leading
fields.note: Purpose undetermined. It occupies the same three bytes a request uses, and a server is free to send zeros there.

fields.name: clientId
fields.note: Which seat in the match the named player occupies, counted from zero.

fields.name: version
fields.note: The build the client said it runs, copied from its request and kept. A server writes nothing here for a seat that was already at the match, and it is zero in everything observed.

fields.name: proof
fields.note: The eight bytes a request fills with its proof. A server puts no meaningful value here, so whatever these carry is not a fact about the protocol. They are zero in everything observed.

fields.name: trailing
fields.note: Four bytes closing the record. Zero in everything observed.
